newsitem.title: USA: Dell unveils workstations at low prices.
newsitem.headline: Dell unveils workstations at low prices.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp said it introduced its first workstations, the Dell WorkStation 400, at aggressive prices, saying it expects to shake up the $15 billon workstation market.
Dell said it introduced the Dell WorkStation 400 with a single 266 megahertz Pentium II processor for $3,705, to a dual processor 300 megahertz Pentium II, for $8,078.
"Today Dell is introducing quite awesome workstations at price points that will set the market on fire," said Linda Hargrove, vice president of workstations, Dell Americas.

Dell executives likened their entree into personal workstations to their entree in the server market last year, which is now at a run rate of about $1 billion in revenues, said Kevin Rollins, president of Dell Americas.
"Our goal is to ramp it in a simliar fashion," Rollins said after a press conference which took place at the NASDAQ, one of Dell's big customers and to emphasize its focus on financial customers.
Rollins would not give any forecasts for Dell's workstation revenues, but he said that he thinks Dell can do even better in workstations than in the server market.
"We see this as a greater opportunity for us than servers," Rollins said.
"Workstations are already sold direct and there is not a dominant player, such as Compaq is in the server market."

Dell said that because workstations are mostly sold directly through computer makers to their customers and they do not go through a distribution channel, they fit in with Dell's direct business model.
